# Time zones given as a UTC offset, which BigQuery's data types reference spells
# (+|-)H[H][:M[M]], such as '-08:00', '-8:15', '+3:00', '+07:30' and '-7'.

# Expected values: the offset applied to the civil time, as the reference defines it.
SELECT CAST(DATETIME(TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00', '-08:00') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-25 07:30:00"

SELECT CAST(DATETIME(TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00', '+07:30') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-25 23:00:00"

SELECT CAST(DATE(TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00', '+9') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-26"

SELECT CAST(TIME(TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00', '-8:15') AS STRING)
=> "07:15:00"

SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00' AT TIME ZONE '+3:00')
=> "18"

SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(DATETIME FROM TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00' AT TIME ZONE '-7') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-25 08:30:00"

SELECT CAST(TIMESTAMP(DATETIME '2008-12-25 15:30:00', '-08:00') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-25 23:30:00+00"

SELECT CAST(TIMESTAMP(DATE '2008-12-25', '+07:30') AS STRING)
=> "2008-12-24 16:30:00+00"

# The time zone is not a literal, so it is read at run time.
SELECT CAST(DATETIME(TIMESTAMP '2008-12-25 15:30:00+00', z) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST(['-08:30']) z
=> "2008-12-25 07:00:00"

# Expected values: BigQuery's answers.

# A civil time repeated at a daylight saving change converts to its earlier instant;
# America/Los_Angeles falls back at 02:00 PDT to 01:00 PST on 2024-11-03.
SELECT CAST(TIMESTAMP(DATETIME '2024-11-03 01:30:00', 'America/Los_Angeles') AS STRING)
=> "2024-11-03 08:30:00+00"

# An unknown time zone that is not a literal.
SELECT CAST(DATETIME(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 12:00:00+00', z) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST(['Invalid/Zone']) z
=> error: Invalid time zone: Invalid/Zone

# A civil time outside the DATETIME range is an error, which SAFE. turns into NULL, but its time
# of day is not.
SELECT CAST(SAFE.DATETIME(TIMESTAMP '0001-01-01 00:00:00+00', '-08:00') AS STRING)
=> null

SELECT CAST(TIME(TIMESTAMP '0001-01-01 00:00:00+00', '-08:00') AS STRING)
=> "16:00:00"
